notes: No breadboard is used: the manual uses ready-made Grove modules on the MKR Connector Carrier (Grove cables).
The Grove connector names on the carrier (A0, D0, D1, TWI) follow the manual: moisture sensor on A0, water sensor on D0, relay on D1, barometric sensor and OLED on TWI via the Grove I2C Hub.
The photo shows the MKR Zero-style board; the manual says MKR Zero. The MKR Zero is modelled as a new part type since it is not in the catalogue.
Grove cable line mapping: SIG = SCL (MKR pin 12), NC = SDA (MKR pin 11) on the TWI connector. Grove VCC is taken from the carrier's 3.3V rail (the carrier's actual VCC voltage selector is not shown).
Because the Grove cable ports are used for electrical edges, the 'joined' edge for each cable end is recorded at connector level (no specific port).

Water sensor hack: two solid wires of different length (difference = minimum water depth, e.g. 10 cm) are soldered to two non-connected tinned bars on the Grove water sensor (modelled as BAR.1 and BAR.2).

12V power circuit (the 'Next step' section) is included: 12V supply to carrier VIN/GND screw terminals, VIN fed to relay COM, relay NO to pump, pump return to GND. The wall-wart has a single PLUG port, so it is connected to both VIN and GND; the exact schematic image was not available so this is inferred from the text.
The pump (or electronic valve) is modelled as a dc-motor. The plant vase/soil and water tank are not modelled as parts.
The USB cable (type A to micro-B) connects the computer running the Arduino IDE to the MKR Zero; the usb-cable catalogue part has no named ports.
